findings.description: The shortcut condition is inverted. It returns the maximum wait when the exponent is below log_base(max/multiplier), which is exactly when the computed wait is still below max. The intended shortcut is for exponent above that threshold, where the result would be clamped to max anyway.
findings.rationale: Trigger: wait_exponential(multiplier=1, max=60) on attempt 1. exponent=0 and log2(60)≈5.9, so 0<5.9 and the shortcut fires, returning 60 instead of 1. Early attempts therefore wait max instead of growing exponentially. Large attempt numbers fall through to the pow computation, which is the cost the change meant to avoid.
